config.label: Your Resy account email
config.description: Your Resy account email. Optional — leave unset to use the fetchproxy browser bridge instead.

config.label: Your Resy account password
config.description: Your Resy account password. Optional — leave unset to use the fetchproxy browser bridge instead.

config.label: Pre-obtained x-resy-auth-token
config.description: Pre-obtained x-resy-auth-token. Overrides email/password and the fetchproxy bridge. Power users / CI only.

config.label: Set to '1' to disable the fetchproxy fallback (forces RESY_EMAIL+PASSWORD or RESY_AUTH_TOKEN)
config.description: Set to '1' to disable the fetchproxy fallback (forces RESY_EMAIL+PASSWORD or RESY_AUTH_TOKEN).

config.label: Pin the api key, beating both the key captured from the live site and the compiled-in default
config.description: Pin the api key, beating both the key captured from the live site and the compiled-in default. Rotation does not require it: the key is captured and cached automatically.

config.label: Set to false to disable the on-disk token cache and re-authenticate on every process start
config.description: Set to false to disable the on-disk token cache and re-authenticate on every process start. Defaults to enabled.

config.label: Absolute path for the token cache file
config.description: Absolute path for the token cache file. Defaults to $MCP_DATA_DIR/.resy-mcp/token.json.

config.label: Absolute path for the api-key cache file
config.description: Absolute path for the api-key cache file. Defaults to $MCP_DATA_DIR/.resy-mcp/api-key.json. Holds the bare key captured from the live site, which takes precedence over the compiled-in default.

config.label: Seconds to wait for the signed-in page to make an API call the bridge can read the auth token from
config.description: Seconds to wait for the signed-in page to make an API call the bridge can read the auth token from. Defaults to 30. Capture resolves on the next matching request, so an idle tab needs a longer window than a busy one.

config.label: Port for the fetchproxy bridge
config.description: Port for the fetchproxy bridge. The whole fleet shares 37149 (the Transporter extension dials it), so override only for local development, test isolation, or a hosted bridged registration — this is the variable to name in the registration's bridgePortEnv.
